approach.method_basis: CMA-ES samples candidate points from a multivariate Gaussian, ranks the ones that come back, and moves the distribution itself rather than any individual point. The mean shifts toward a weighted average of the better samples, the covariance matrix adapts so the Gaussian stretches along directions that have been paying off, and a separate cumulative path controls the overall step size. Applied to molecules, the sampled points are latent vectors and each one is turned into a molecule by a frozen autoencoder decoder before scoring.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a 24-dimensional latent with full covariance adaptation rather than a diagonal approximation, so the Gaussian can learn correlated directions in the latent space. It attaches every observed score to the exact latent sample that generated the molecule, uses descending score rank with logarithmic recombination weights, and carries cumulative evolution paths for both covariance and step size across all fourteen generations of an objective.

hypothesis: Sample de novo molecules through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE decoder from an adaptive multivariate Gaussian, attach observed scores to the exact generating latent samples, and update the Gaussian mean, full covariance, and global step size using descending score ranks, weighted recombination, and cumulative evolution paths.

finding_summary.headline: Full covariance adaptation ran exactly and finished eleventh at 0.303, undone by one objective
finding_summary.insights: The optimizer is correct and its budget is the problem. Fourteen generations of twenty scored offspring is a very short run for an algorithm that spends its early generations learning a covariance, so the distribution barely finishes adapting before the budget ends. Its collapse on drd2_docking is informative in a different way: that objective rewards a compact basic amine, and this node's proposals there average eighty characters, nearly double every other objective on the same node. The Gaussian drifted into a region of latent space that decodes to large lipophilic molecules and covariance adaptation then reinforced that direction. A smaller population with more generations is the obvious change. One seed only.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.303 places this eleventh of thirteen. The result is bimodal: 0.611 on deco_hop, which is the third best in the round, and 0.443 on zaleplon_mpo, against 0.064 on drd2_docking, which is the second worst any root recorded there. median_2 reached 0.208 and sitagliptin_mpo 0.187. Every mechanism check was exact. All 70 generations used full 24 by 24 covariance matrices with reconstructed rank-one and rank-mu terms, the recomputed learning constants matched, the cumulative path and step-size control were independently reproduced through eigendecomposition of each covariance, and every one of the accepted offspring joined its exact generating latent and score.

molecular.headline: Latent drift into large lipophilic molecules, with aromatic content collapsing on the objectives it loses
molecular.overall_character: The population varies more by objective than any other root, which is what covariance adaptation in a latent space would be expected to produce. Where it does well, aromatic content reaches 86 to 95 percent with molecules around forty to fifty-nine characters. Where it fails, aromatic content drops to 36 and 49 percent and molecules balloon to eighty characters of fluorinated ethers and alkyl chains. Ring closure stays high throughout at 87 to 99 percent, so the decoder is producing closed structures; what changes is whether those rings are aromatic and whether the molecule stays a reasonable size.

per_task.generated_character: Fused acridine-like amides averaging forty-one characters with 86 percent aromatic content, but the lowest halogen rate on the node at 8 percent.
liabilities: cyclic imine bridges hydrolyse under physiological conditions
enol ether termini appear throughout and are acid labile
missing_features: halogen substitution, present in under a tenth of proposals
stable ring fusions rather than the imine bridges in the top scorers
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best at 0.443 is a diarylamine fused through an imine into a tricyclic, and it is the node's second strongest objective. The zero scorers are large open chains carrying multiple amide and ester groups, so the latent region here stayed compact where on other objectives it did not.

per_task.generated_character: The node's best objective and third best in the round. Halogenated benzamides linked to fused polyaza aromatics, averaging fifty-nine characters with 94 percent aromatic content and near-total ring closure.
liabilities: chains of three and four consecutive N=C imine bonds are not stable functional groups
an alpha-keto ester in the top scorer is hydrolytically labile
missing_features: stable amide linkers in place of the repeated N=C imine chains in the high scorers
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top four cluster between 0.595 and 0.611 and all share a substituted benzoate amide joined to a nitrogen-rich fused ring. The bottom of the range drops the fused aromatic for sulfone-bridged enones. Where the latent Gaussian stayed in aromatic territory, this method performs well.

per_task.generated_character: The clearest failure on this node. Proposals average eighty characters, nearly double every other objective here, with only 49 percent aromatic content and long fluorinated alkyl and ether chains dominating.
liabilities: extended perfluoroalkyl chains carry no drug-likeness and high lipophilicity
geminal diols and hemiketal-like centres appear among the top scorers
missing_features: a protonatable aliphatic amine, absent from the entire top of the range
compact molecules; this set averages eighty characters against forty for the winners
simple fused aromatic bicyclics such as indoles
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The whole population spans 0.0002 to 0.064, so there is no gradient to climb. Not one proposal carries the basic amine on a compact aromatic that other roots used to reach above 0.9. The top scorers are large spirocyclic ethers with pendant fluorophenyl chains, which is the wrong region entirely.

per_task.generated_character: The node's most aromatic set at 95 percent with ring closure at 99.7 percent, averaging forty-nine characters of benzodioxole-substituted biaryls and fused lactams, and almost no halogen at 5 percent.
liabilities: cross-conjugated ketoamides among the low scorers are reactive
missing_features: molecules positioned between the two similarity targets rather than near one
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best at 0.208 is the third highest on this objective in the round, and it is also the smallest molecule in its own top four, a simple ethoxyphenyl benzodioxole. Scores fall away into open conjugated amides, so compactness and ring content are what the objective is rewarding here.

per_task.generated_character: Only 36 percent of proposals carry an aromatic atom and 13 percent close no ring, averaging thirty-six characters of partially saturated conjugated rings and open enones.
liabilities: acrylamide and cross-conjugated enone groups are Michael acceptors
terpenoid-like polycyclic hydrocarbons are not candidates for this objective
missing_features: aromatic rings, absent from nearly two thirds of proposals
fluorinated substituents, present in only 13 percent of proposals
stereochemistry, absent from all 290 proposals
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best reaches 0.187 against a median of 0.0001. The top entries are small partially saturated pyridines and acrylamides, while the zero scorers are large terpenoid and steroid-like polycycles with long alkyl chains, which is the same latent drift toward lipophilic bulk seen on the objective it lost.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On the objective it loses worst, proposals average eighty characters against thirty-six to fifty-nine on the same node's other objectives, with aromatic content falling to 49 percent and long perfluoroalkyl chains dominating the top of the range.
transferable_gaps.gap: the sampling distribution drifts into large lipophilic regions and then reinforces the drift
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Adapting a covariance on ranked samples amplifies whatever direction the early generations happened to favour, so a bad early drift becomes self-reinforcing rather than self-correcting. A bound on the sampled region, or a restart when the population's character shifts, is what this asks for.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each objective completed exactly fourteen generations of twenty scored offspring, while a full 24 by 24 covariance with rank-one and rank-mu updates needs far more to become informative.
transferable_gaps.gap: the search has too few generations to finish adapting its covariance
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Spending a fixed budget on twenty samples per generation buys covariance estimates that never converge. Fewer samples per generation and more generations would let the adaptation mechanism actually do its work within the same number of evaluations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The second and third highest-scoring molecules on one objective each carry three or four consecutive N=C linkages in a single chain, and similar chains appear throughout that population.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator writes chains of consecutive imine bonds
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The decoder can repeat an imine token indefinitely because nothing checks that the resulting chain is a real functional group. Capping consecutive heteroatom double bonds at emission removes these without constraining the latent search.

method_name: CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder
method_thesis: Anchor the optimizer in CMA-ES: sample a multivariate Gaussian, rank evaluated samples, move its mean by weighted recombination, and adapt covariance and step size using selected displacements and cumulative evolution paths. [Hansen, Sections 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1604.00772v2) describes this mechanism. For the molecular transfer, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder. Each objective starts with fresh Gaussian and path state. Encodings of high-scoring supplied molecules may initialize geometric search locations, but their scores must not be assigned to nonidentical reconstructions. Generate latent samples, decode them into new molecules, and attach accepted oracle feedback to the exact latent sample that produced each submitted structure. Assemble scored generations while respecting the evaluator-announced batching, then update the Gaussian from descending observed-score ranks. Reject invalid or duplicate structures locally and continue de novo decoding. The corpus trains a generator and never supplies a ranked molecular library. The hypothesis is that learning correlated latent displacements directly from successful generations can uncover improving combinations without first estimating an objective surrogate, increasing the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Useful decoder support and covariance adaptation within scarce feedback are empirical prerequisites; continuous-domain performance is not evidence that decoded molecular landscapes will behave similarly.

activation_observables.measurement: At every complete generation log each accepted member's canonical identity, exact sampled latent, observed score, rank and recombination weight, plus the old and new mean and effective selection mass. Recompute the weighted selected displacement and mean update, report its numerical residual and displacement norm, and report weighted selected score minus the full-generation mean as rank-selection enrichment. activation_observables.name: observed_rank_weighted_mean_updates

activation_observables.measurement: Log the old and new full covariance matrices, cumulative covariance path, rank-one and rank-mu contributions, learning constants and any positive-definiteness correction at every update. Reconstruct the update and report its residual, path norm, covariance displacement, off-diagonal Frobenius norm, eigenvalue range and condition number relative to the initialized identity covariance. Join the resulting covariance version and factor to the next generation's sampling receipts. Nonzero contributions that alter the sampled covariance establish directional adaptation; a computed matrix that is never used does not.
activation_observables.name: full_covariance_evolution_path_adaptation

activation_observables.measurement: Log the old and new step sizes, whitened recombination displacement, old and new cumulative step-size path, its norm, the reference Gaussian norm, damping and cumulation constants, raw multiplicative update, and every safeguard activation. Reconstruct the cumulative path and step-size arithmetic, then join the resulting step size to the next generation's samples. Expected behavior is a nonzero path and realized scale adaptation from its initial value; no universal increase or decrease is predicted.

research_intent.falsifier: The intended CMA mechanism is refuted if feedback is attached to a re-encoded or reconstructed molecule instead of the exact latent that generated the scored submission, frozen neural weights change, decoder randomness supplies an undeclared proposal mechanism, or emitted molecules come from a finite library or non-Gaussian structural mutation. Incorrect rank membership, absent weighted mean movement despite nondegenerate selected displacements, missing covariance/path terms, isotropic-only replacement of the declared full covariance update, or cumulative step-size state that is computed but never used refutes the corresponding adaptation component. Incomplete terminal generations must be distinguished from skipped complete-generation updates. Failure to reduce heldout reconstruction NLL refutes the learned-generator prerequisite; inability to fill valid novel batches through the Gaussian decoder refutes generative viability. Missing receipts make activation inconclusive. Imperfect initial reconstruction, poor latent distance alignment or no final Top-1 improvement alone does not refute an otherwise correctly activated frozen-decoder CMA process; those are representation or score limitations to retain as evidence.
research_intent.implementation_change: Implement an import-safe optimize.py with unlabeled preparation and clean independent objective sessions. Train a compact SELFIES VAE from scratch on a seeded subset of the permitted corpus using reconstruction and KL losses, with a fixed holdout excluded from optimization. Use an encoder with a continuous Gaussian posterior and a latent-conditioned sequence decoder; reserve deterministic greedy decoding for run mode. Select a reusable checkpoint using heldout reconstruction performance, and publish encoder/decoder weights, vocabulary, latent normalization and configuration without retaining a molecular candidate pool. During run, seed every used RNG from init, route tensor work to logical cuda:0, load the checkpoint in evaluation mode, and freeze all encoder and decoder parameters. Initialize one fresh full-covariance CMA state with positive step size and zero cumulative paths. High-scoring supplied molecules may determine its initial geometric mean through frozen encoder posterior means, but no initial molecule's score enters a scored CMA generation through its reconstruction, even when reconstruction happens to match. Keep initial observations in the identity and best-result archive. Choose a small generation size appropriate to latent dimension and round it to an integer multiple of the evaluator-announced suggestion batch size. Freeze Gaussian parameters while gathering one generation across protocol batches; every suggest still emits exactly the announced size. Draw fresh standard-normal vectors, transform them using the current Gaussian covariance factor and step size, and deterministically decode the resulting exact latent vectors. Validate and canonicalize by reparsing the decoded SMILES, reject invalid or repeated structures locally, and refill exclusively with fresh Gaussian latent draws through that same decoder. Store each original submitted identity, canonical identity, exact sampled latent, Gaussian version and sampling displacement before sending it. Match feedback first to the echoed submitted identity and retain its canonical identity for novelty. Once a full generation has accepted real scores, rank those samples in descending score order and apply positive logarithmic recombination weights, a cumulative covariance path, rank-one and rank-mu covariance updates, and cumulative step-size adaptation as in [Hansen Sections 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1604.00772v2). Use numerical symmetry, positive-eigenvalue and finite-step-size safeguards with every correction logged. The next generation must sample the updated parameters. Retain terminal partial-generation observations in the best-result archive and log their incomplete update status; never invent missing scores. Bound preparation, decoding and matrix workloads to the supplied runtime profile, handle stop silently, and emit structured stderr receipts for all registered observables. Log nearby latent and decoded-fingerprint distances descriptively to inform the proposal's conditional representation improvement, without using those distances to rank proposals. This root adds no objective surrogate, online neural adaptation, fingerprint-distance training loss, graph mutation, token mutation, finite molecule library or score transfer across decoder mismatches.
research_intent.mechanism: Sample de novo molecules through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE decoder from an adaptive multivariate Gaussian, attach observed scores to the exact generating latent samples, and update the Gaussian mean, full covariance, and global step size using descending score ranks, weighted recombination, and cumulative evolution paths.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: This lineage has no Parent or evaluated CMA-ES root. Its difficulty is to learn useful correlated search directions from scarce molecular feedback in a latent space whose decoded objective may be discontinuous or highly redundant. The supplied node n-77c41c9bc036 was refuted when online flow adaptation broke its registered exact-token reconstruction invariant, although the failed checks retained canonical molecular identity. That evidence motivates freezing this root's representation and auditing score-to-decoded-sample attachment; it does not establish that a VAE has useful local geometry or that CMA-ES will improve scores.

applicability_conditions: Activation is supported for this root's screening seed 0 on the five supplied independent scalar molecular maximization tasks, using the frozen 24-dimensional learned VAE, 10 initial observations, batches of 10 and scored generations of 20. There is no Parent comparison or multi-seed reliability evidence.

Each objective starts with a fresh Gaussian, identity covariance, sigma 0.9, zero paths, pending state and archive. Only the matching unlabeled prepared checkpoint and its fixed normalization are shared; objective feedback changes only the CMA state and within-objective archive.

Gaussian decoder support was sufficient for all 145 valid novel batches. Validity/novelty rejection and excess truncation condition the accepted distribution, so these receipts establish the implemented filtered molecular CMA process and not an unfiltered continuous-domain invariance result.

Scored offspring are accepted only through their exact generating-latent receipts, with deterministic identity rechecks and fixed neural tensors. Imperfect reconstruction of initially supplied molecules does not transfer their original scores to a generation.

All three adaptation components moved and were used in subsequent samples within 14 complete generations per task. The final 10 scored offspring per task affect the result archive and correctly remain an incomplete generation.

Observed activation and positive within-generation rank enrichment do not isolate a final-score contribution relative to a frozen-Gaussian ablation. Broad within-generation geometry diagnostics do not establish a locally smooth decoder landscape or the proposed later fingerprint-distance regularizer's benefit.

finding_summary.insights: The optimizer is correct and its budget is the problem. molecular_assessment.headline: Latent drift into large lipophilic molecules, with aromatic content collapsing on the objectives it loses
molecular_assessment.overall_character: The population varies more by objective than any other root, which is what covariance adaptation in a latent space would be expected to produce. Where it does well, aromatic content reaches 86 to 95 percent with molecules around forty to fifty-nine characters. Where it fails, aromatic content drops to 36 and 49 percent and molecules balloon to eighty characters of fluorinated ethers and alkyl chains. Ring closure stays high throughout at 87 to 99 percent, so the decoder is producing closed structures; what changes is whether those rings are aromatic and whether the molecule stays a reasonable size.

per_task.generated_character: Fused acridine-like amides averaging forty-one characters with 86 percent aromatic content, but the lowest halogen rate on the node at 8 percent.
liabilities: cyclic imine bridges hydrolyse under physiological conditions
enol ether termini appear throughout and are acid labile
missing_features: halogen substitution, present in under a tenth of proposals
stable ring fusions rather than the imine bridges in the top scorers
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best at 0.443 is a diarylamine fused through an imine into a tricyclic, and it is the node's second strongest objective. The zero scorers are large open chains carrying multiple amide and ester groups, so the latent region here stayed compact where on other objectives it did not.

per_task.generated_character: The node's best objective and third best in the round. Halogenated benzamides linked to fused polyaza aromatics, averaging fifty-nine characters with 94 percent aromatic content and near-total ring closure.
liabilities: chains of three and four consecutive N=C imine bonds are not stable functional groups
an alpha-keto ester in the top scorer is hydrolytically labile
missing_features: stable amide linkers in place of the repeated N=C imine chains in the high scorers
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top four cluster between 0.595 and 0.611 and all share a substituted benzoate amide joined to a nitrogen-rich fused ring. The bottom of the range drops the fused aromatic for sulfone-bridged enones. Where the latent Gaussian stayed in aromatic territory, this method performs well.

per_task.generated_character: The clearest failure on this node. Proposals average eighty characters, nearly double every other objective here, with only 49 percent aromatic content and long fluorinated alkyl and ether chains dominating.
liabilities: extended perfluoroalkyl chains carry no drug-likeness and high lipophilicity
geminal diols and hemiketal-like centres appear among the top scorers
missing_features: a protonatable aliphatic amine, absent from the entire top of the range
compact molecules; this set averages eighty characters against forty for the winners
simple fused aromatic bicyclics such as indoles
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The whole population spans 0.0002 to 0.064, so there is no gradient to climb. Not one proposal carries the basic amine on a compact aromatic that other roots used to reach above 0.9. The top scorers are large spirocyclic ethers with pendant fluorophenyl chains, which is the wrong region entirely.

per_task.generated_character: The node's most aromatic set at 95 percent with ring closure at 99.7 percent, averaging forty-nine characters of benzodioxole-substituted biaryls and fused lactams, and almost no halogen at 5 percent.
liabilities: cross-conjugated ketoamides among the low scorers are reactive
missing_features: molecules positioned between the two similarity targets rather than near one
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best at 0.208 is the third highest on this objective in the round, and it is also the smallest molecule in its own top four, a simple ethoxyphenyl benzodioxole. Scores fall away into open conjugated amides, so compactness and ring content are what the objective is rewarding here.

per_task.generated_character: Only 36 percent of proposals carry an aromatic atom and 13 percent close no ring, averaging thirty-six characters of partially saturated conjugated rings and open enones.
liabilities: acrylamide and cross-conjugated enone groups are Michael acceptors
terpenoid-like polycyclic hydrocarbons are not candidates for this objective
missing_features: aromatic rings, absent from nearly two thirds of proposals
fluorinated substituents, present in only 13 percent of proposals
stereochemistry, absent from all 290 proposals
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best reaches 0.187 against a median of 0.0001. The top entries are small partially saturated pyridines and acrylamides, while the zero scorers are large terpenoid and steroid-like polycycles with long alkyl chains, which is the same latent drift toward lipophilic bulk seen on the objective it lost.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On the objective it loses worst, proposals average eighty characters against thirty-six to fifty-nine on the same node's other objectives, with aromatic content falling to 49 percent and long perfluoroalkyl chains dominating the top of the range.
transferable_gaps.gap: the sampling distribution drifts into large lipophilic regions and then reinforces the drift
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Adapting a covariance on ranked samples amplifies whatever direction the early generations happened to favour, so a bad early drift becomes self-reinforcing rather than self-correcting. A bound on the sampled region, or a restart when the population's character shifts, is what this asks for.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each objective completed exactly fourteen generations of twenty scored offspring, while a full 24 by 24 covariance with rank-one and rank-mu updates needs far more to become informative.
transferable_gaps.gap: the search has too few generations to finish adapting its covariance
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Spending a fixed budget on twenty samples per generation buys covariance estimates that never converge. Fewer samples per generation and more generations would let the adaptation mechanism actually do its work within the same number of evaluations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The second and third highest-scoring molecules on one objective each carry three or four consecutive N=C linkages in a single chain, and similar chains appear throughout that population.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator writes chains of consecutive imine bonds
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The decoder can repeat an imine token indefinitely because nothing checks that the resulting chain is a real functional group. Capping consecutive heteroatom double bonds at emission removes these without constraining the latent search.

possible_failure_causes: The learned representation has low greedy exact/canonical reconstruction, 6/480, and all 15 selected initial encodings across the task sessions decode to different canonical molecules. This may weaken geometric initialization from high-scoring observations, despite the verified absence of score transfer.

Within-generation diagnostic fingerprint distances are generally large, and task-level descriptive Pearson correlations between latent and fingerprint distance range from 0.0349783776276 to 0.234549528935. These observations suggest weak distance alignment as a possible search limitation, but the pairs are dependent and not a controlled nearby-latent probe; they do not establish the benefit of distance-preserving preparation.

applicability_conditions: Applies to independent scalar molecular maximization tasks when permitted unlabeled preparation learns a deterministic decoder with enough valid, distinct output support for repeated Gaussian sampling.

The compact latent dimension and chosen generation size must permit covariance and cumulative-path learning within the supplied feedback. Continuous-domain CMA performance does not establish usefulness on a discontinuous decoded molecular landscape.

All neural weights and latent normalization remain frozen during each objective. Initialization can use observed-score preferences over encoder locations without assigning the original scores to decoded reconstructions.

Accepted offspring scores are joined to the exact latent samples that produced their submitted canonical identities. Multiple latents that decode to the same molecule are locally deduplicated and do not create extra labeled offspring.

Validity and novelty filtering change the distribution of accepted samples. The root retains the CMA update mechanism but claims no unfiltered-Gaussian sampling theorem or invariance guarantee for the filtered molecular search.
All Gaussian parameters, paths, archives and pending generations restart for every objective; only the unlabeled prepared representation is shared.

Node n-77c41c9bc036 concerns a different adaptable flow architecture and a stricter exact-token invariant. Its refutation does not establish failure or success of this frozen VAE root, and no settled Mechanism Cluster is being revisited.

The distance-preserving preparation change from the method proposal remains a conditional later experiment. Root geometry diagnostics and screening-seed scores cannot establish that change's benefit or multi-seed reliability.

approach.method_basis: CMA-ES samples candidate points from a multivariate Gaussian, ranks the ones that come back, and moves the distribution itself rather than any individual point. The mean shifts toward a weighted average of the better samples, the covariance matrix adapts so the Gaussian stretches along directions that have been paying off, and a separate cumulative path controls the overall step size. Applied to molecules, the sampled points are latent vectors and each one is turned into a molecule by a frozen autoencoder decoder before scoring.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a 24-dimensional latent with full covariance adaptation rather than a diagonal approximation, so the Gaussian can learn correlated directions in the latent space. It attaches every observed score to the exact latent sample that generated the molecule, uses descending score rank with logarithmic recombination weights, and carries cumulative evolution paths for both covariance and step size across all fourteen generations of an objective.

research_intent.falsifier: The intended CMA mechanism is refuted if feedback is attached to a re-encoded or reconstructed molecule instead of the exact latent that generated the scored submission, frozen neural weights change, decoder randomness supplies an undeclared proposal mechanism, or emitted molecules come from a finite library or non-Gaussian structural mutation. Incorrect rank membership, absent weighted mean movement despite nondegenerate selected displacements, missing covariance/path terms, isotropic-only replacement of the declared full covariance update, or cumulative step-size state that is computed but never used refutes the corresponding adaptation component. Incomplete terminal generations must be distinguished from skipped complete-generation updates. Failure to reduce heldout reconstruction NLL refutes the learned-generator prerequisite; inability to fill valid novel batches through the Gaussian decoder refutes generative viability. Missing receipts make activation inconclusive. Imperfect initial reconstruction, poor latent distance alignment or no final Top-1 improvement alone does not refute an otherwise correctly activated frozen-decoder CMA process; those are representation or score limitations to retain as evidence.
research_intent.implementation_change: Implement an import-safe optimize.py with unlabeled preparation and clean independent objective sessions. Train a compact SELFIES VAE from scratch on a seeded subset of the permitted corpus using reconstruction and KL losses, with a fixed holdout excluded from optimization. Use an encoder with a continuous Gaussian posterior and a latent-conditioned sequence decoder; reserve deterministic greedy decoding for run mode. Select a reusable checkpoint using heldout reconstruction performance, and publish encoder/decoder weights, vocabulary, latent normalization and configuration without retaining a molecular candidate pool. During run, seed every used RNG from init, route tensor work to logical cuda:0, load the checkpoint in evaluation mode, and freeze all encoder and decoder parameters. Initialize one fresh full-covariance CMA state with positive step size and zero cumulative paths. High-scoring supplied molecules may determine its initial geometric mean through frozen encoder posterior means, but no initial molecule's score enters a scored CMA generation through its reconstruction, even when reconstruction happens to match. Keep initial observations in the identity and best-result archive. Choose a small generation size appropriate to latent dimension and round it to an integer multiple of the evaluator-announced suggestion batch size. Freeze Gaussian parameters while gathering one generation across protocol batches; every suggest still emits exactly the announced size. Draw fresh standard-normal vectors, transform them using the current Gaussian covariance factor and step size, and deterministically decode the resulting exact latent vectors. Validate and canonicalize by reparsing the decoded SMILES, reject invalid or repeated structures locally, and refill exclusively with fresh Gaussian latent draws through that same decoder. Store each original submitted identity, canonical identity, exact sampled latent, Gaussian version and sampling displacement before sending it. Match feedback first to the echoed submitted identity and retain its canonical identity for novelty. Once a full generation has accepted real scores, rank those samples in descending score order and apply positive logarithmic recombination weights, a cumulative covariance path, rank-one and rank-mu covariance updates, and cumulative step-size adaptation as in [Hansen Sections 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1604.00772v2). Use numerical symmetry, positive-eigenvalue and finite-step-size safeguards with every correction logged. The next generation must sample the updated parameters. Retain terminal partial-generation observations in the best-result archive and log their incomplete update status; never invent missing scores. Bound preparation, decoding and matrix workloads to the supplied runtime profile, handle stop silently, and emit structured stderr receipts for all registered observables. Log nearby latent and decoded-fingerprint distances descriptively to inform the proposal's conditional representation improvement, without using those distances to rank proposals. This root adds no objective surrogate, online neural adaptation, fingerprint-distance training loss, graph mutation, token mutation, finite molecule library or score transfer across decoder mismatches.
research_intent.mechanism: Sample de novo molecules through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE decoder from an adaptive multivariate Gaussian, attach observed scores to the exact generating latent samples, and update the Gaussian mean, full covariance, and global step size using descending score ranks, weighted recombination, and cumulative evolution paths.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: This lineage has no Parent or evaluated CMA-ES root. Its difficulty is to learn useful correlated search directions from scarce molecular feedback in a latent space whose decoded objective may be discontinuous or highly redundant. The supplied node n-77c41c9bc036 was refuted when online flow adaptation broke its registered exact-token reconstruction invariant, although the failed checks retained canonical molecular identity. That evidence motivates freezing this root's representation and auditing score-to-decoded-sample attachment; it does not establish that a VAE has useful local geometry or that CMA-ES will improve scores.
